Q: How does for i in range() works A:

In Python, doing for i in range(x): will make the indented code following the for statement run x number of times. It can also be written as for i in range(start, stop, step): where the start and step arguments are optional. i here will start at start , will increase by step , and will end at (not including) stop .

For example, the code

for i in range(10):
  print(i)

will print all numbers from 0 to 9.

Q: Implicit number-to-string conversion in Perl A:

This is not a problem hidden in sprintf, it's a general problem in how floating point numbers are represented in computer systems. Your eyes see a decimal numbers but they are converted in binary format in computers. This is specified in IEEE 754. You can have 32 bit, 64 bit or may be higher precision, but some numbers don't have exact representation from decimal digit to binary floating point. I'm surprised that many people are not aware. The standard is defined many years ago and when I was a student in previous century we were studied to be careful with it.

Easiest way to explain is the 0.1 is a famous example.
--------------------
You can test the following:
print ((0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3)?'YES':'NO');

Surprise! You will have printed NO
It's because 0.1 doesn't have exact floating point representation.
0.1 in 64-bit: 0.1000000000000000055511151231257827021181583404541015625

Read the standard please and you will find exactly how floating numbers are represented. Explaining the standard here is a nonsense because it is widely available.

Q: running a spark submit job as cluster deploy mode fails but passes with client A:

If you have already your yarn cluster installed and configured you just need to set HADOOP_CONF_DIR environment variable to point to your client hadoop configuration. You don't need specify those aws jars since they are already provided by your hadoop cluster. So if you provide them again they could conflict with the ones already there. Reference the documentation here for the spark submit. Also I would suggest to use s3n as protocol to read and write from S3.
